source.title: Apply evidence, novelty, bounty and submission requirements across all problem work
source.body:
Establish and apply one evidence and submission standard across **all problem work in grwtsk/math**, including Erdős problems, imported proofs, original results, partial results and computational claims.

User instruction: record the requirements from https://erdosproblemaday.com/guide as a general repository issue, resolve them across our problems, and submit eligible work once a bounty is earned. Submission endpoint: https://erdosproblemaday.com/submit. Read the current destination rules again before any submission.

## Required problem record

- [ ] Record the authoritative problem identity, exact quantifiers/hypotheses, variants, and whether the result is full, partial, conditional or computational.
- [ ] Check current literature and primary sources; retain stable references and dates. Distinguish original contributions from imported proofs, reformulations and formalization bridges.
- [ ] Supply a readable, checkable exposition, citations, artifacts and precise AI-role/version disclosure. Explicitly identify which verification was independent and its limits.
- [ ] For numerical or finite claims, provide reproducible certificates, coverage arguments and independent checks with acceptance/rejection controls where applicable. A finite table does not prove an unbounded statement.
- [ ] Preserve unresolved premises and missing bridges. Avoid claiming human mathematical review when none occurred.

## Repository-specific acceptance

- [ ] Bind every acceptance claim to immutable source commits/blobs, dependency/toolchain identities, exact commands and retained receipt digests.
- [ ] Keep source publication, compilation, fresh kernel checking, transitive axiom audits, expected-statement consumers and host restoration as separate facets; require all applicable facets together.
- [ ] Use explicit NOT_RUN, failed, pending and accepted statuses. Neither progress, a queue completion nor source review establishes acceptance.
- [ ] Follow the paper-to-formalization reference requirements and preserve upstream authorship/licenses. Local content attribution is `grwtsk contributors`. Local automation on behalf of this checkout owner uses `grwtsk <contributors@grwtsk.invalid>`; preserve other contributors’ own author/committer identities and do not enforce or rewrite identities repository-wide.
- [ ] Keep pure mathematics and static acceptance specifications in math; effectful tooling, attempts, receipts, scheduler state and submission machinery belong in grwtsk/noeaaeue.

## Bounty and submission gate

- [ ] Establish the actual prize/bounty terms, eligibility, exact result scope, prior-publication/priority rules and evidence that a bounty has been earned. Kernel verification alone is not bounty eligibility; porting an existing proof is not an original solution.
- [ ] Prepare a complete submission package with exact statement, known work, claimed contribution, readable proof, reproducibility instructions, source pins/verification evidence and AI disclosures.
- [ ] User has authorized submission once a bounty is earned. Preserve that condition; do not submit an unverified result or claim an earned bounty without evidence.
- [ ] The linked submission form requires a reply email and separately offers public-publication consent. Obtain missing contact information when needed; do not infer public consent or invent personal details.
- [ ] Record destination, submitted package identity, delivery/readback, review verdict and subsequent corrections without conflating submission, review, publication and bounty payment.

## Rollout and completion

- [ ] Inventory existing problem entries and classify gaps without upgrading historical evidence.
- [ ] Define a reusable subject-independent checklist/static schema and Noe-owned operational workflow.
- [ ] Apply it to existing work and future imports/proofs; link per-problem remediation issues.
- [ ] Demonstrate the workflow on a complete source-bound example and retain negative controls for missing evidence.
- [ ] Close only when the general workflow is implemented and the inventory has explicit dispositions.

Current prerequisite: #1433 tracks #138's kth-root statement. Complete its proof, exact-statement consumer and three transitive axiom audits before importing more conjectures. The authorized fresh 4 GiB run is pending Noe ownership. No bounty or submission is claimed for #138's existing OpenAI proof port.


## Preferred community source and upstream contribution route

User selected https://github.com/teorth/erdosproblems as the preferred community tracker. Use its current CONTRIBUTING.md and pin the database revision used for each assessment; keep erdosproblems.com as the authoritative problem wording. The earlier third-party guide remains supplementary.

- [ ] Read data/problems.yaml for problem/prize metadata. A listed prize is not evidence of eligibility, award or payment.
- [ ] Keep informal solution status, formal proof status and formalized statement status distinct; preserve source dates and unresolved multipart scope.
- [ ] For appropriate upstream metadata contributions, prepare PRs against data/problems.yaml with proof/source links and methodology. Do not hand-edit generated status, formalized fields or README tables; run the current required validation.
- [ ] Place formal proof links and explanatory notes in formal_status.url/note. Follow upstream limits on brief comments.
- [ ] Recheck live literature, existing proof links and pending contributions before proposing changes. Do not claim a new solution for a port of prior work.
- [ ] Use the destination's current instructions for the actual contribution type. A database PR does not itself submit a bounty claim or establish mathematical acceptance.

References: https://github.com/teorth/erdosproblems/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md and https://github.com/teorth/erdosproblems/blob/main/README.md . This preference does not change the #138 prerequisite or authorize an unsupported status claim.
